how_read: Pages read with scripts/kb/fetch_wiki_live_pages.py (--api https://www.mariowiki.com/api.php --titles ...). The wiki refused the reader's by-revision render call, and the reader fell back by itself to asking for the page by title, checking that the revision it rendered is the revision it had looked up; the revision below is the one the reader printed for each page. Every quoted fragment was checked, by script, to occur word for word in the fetched page text (whitespace collapsed). The pages are kept in build/wiki-live/mariowiki/ in the helper's copy. Where a page covers the whole series, a line uses only what the page says about Yoshi's Story.

lines.line: Summary: The boss at the end of the level Frustration. He paces across his room, and pots and pans fall from the ceiling while he does.

quoted: In Yoshi's Story, Don Bongo is fought at the end of Stage 3-4: Frustration. He attacks by stomping back and forth across the room, causing pots and pans to rain down from the ceiling.

lines.line: Weak points: Three egg hits on his lips beat him. An egg that lands on the rest of his body bounces away.

quoted: a Baby Yoshi has to hit him in the lips three times; hitting him anywhere else simply causes the egg to bounce off his blubber.

lines.line: Looks like: A plump, dragon-like creature with green skin, yellow spots, thick red lips and a striped yellow belly.

quoted: He is a pudgy dragon-like creature with green skin, yellow spots, big red lips, a yellow stomach with stripes, and a big orange-and-yellow belly button.

lines.line: Tips: Walking into him costs no health, because you just bounce off. Only the things falling from the ceiling can hurt you.

quoted: The Baby Yoshi does not lose any health if he touches Don Bongo, simply bouncing off him instead. Only the items falling from the ceiling can hurt the Baby Yoshi.

lines.line: Tips: Each hit makes his lips swell, which gives you a slightly easier target, but once they have been hit twice he moves much faster.

quoted: After each hit, Don Bongo's lips swell, making them a somewhat easier target, although his movement becomes a lot faster after his lips are hit twice.

lines.line: Summary: A genie made of smoke that you face once the level Poochy & Nippy has its 30 fruits eaten. He sends spiked balls rolling down slippery see-saws and breathes fire.

quoted: He is a smoke djinn that was sent by Baby Bowser to patrol the mountains of Yoshi's Island in Yoshi's Story. As such, a Yoshi must fight him after collecting 30 fruits in Stage 3-3: Poochy & Nippy. He attacks by using large spiked balls and causes them to roll down slippery teeter-totters, and breathes fire at the Yoshi.

lines.line: Weak points: Aim for his stomach with three eggs, and only while his body is solid.

quoted: Hitting his stomach with three eggs (while he is tangible) defeats him.
A Yoshi's egg can harm Cloudjin while he is tangible

lines.line: Looks like: A giant genie made of smoke that floats about.

quoted: A giant, wind-bending genie that floats around.
He is a smoke djinn

lines.line: Tips: Only the Japanese release makes him flash red when an egg hurts him, so in other releases that flash is not a sign to look for.

quoted: Cloudjin flashes red when hurt in the Japanese version only.
causing him to flash red (though not in international releases).

lines.line: Summary: A ghost boss at the end of The Tall Tower. He goes invisible and tries to bump into Yoshi while he calls in Peepers.

quoted: He is at the end of The Tall Tower.
Inviso attacks by turning invisible and trying to bump into a Yoshi while summoning Peepers.

lines.line: Weak points: It takes three egg hits to beat him.

quoted: The Yoshi can defeat Inviso by hitting him with three eggs.

lines.line: Looks like: He is see-through, and the only sign of him is the surroundings reflected on his body.

quoted: Inviso's appearance is somewhat hidden, as he is invisible (minus the fact that the world reflects on him).

lines.line: Tips: An egg that strips a Peeper of its feathers makes it fall, and eating it at that point heals Yoshi fully.

quoted: When a Peeper is shot down, a puff of smoke appears, and the Peeper loses its feathers and falls away. If a Yoshi eats a Peeper when it loses its feathers, it will heal him back to full health.
In addition, Inviso summons Peepers during his boss battle.
If a Yoshi shoots one with an egg, it will lose its feathers and fall down.

lines.line: Summary: A vast, cheerful cloud made of yellow candy floss, fought at the end of the level Cloud Cruising.

quoted: fought at the end of Cloud Cruising. She is a colossal, buoyant, smiling cloud composed of fluffy yellow cotton candy.

lines.line: Weak points: You lick her instead of hitting her. Each lick takes a piece off, and she is beaten once she has been eaten up.

quoted: In order to defeat Cloud N. Candy, a Yoshi has to lick her, which will pick off pieces of her, causing her to shrink until she is fully eaten.

lines.line: Looks like: A very large floating cloud with a smile on it, yellow and fluffy like candy floss.

quoted: She is a colossal, buoyant, smiling cloud composed of fluffy yellow cotton candy.

lines.line: Tips: She leaps around and hurts you if you touch her, and the smaller she gets the faster and nimbler she is. Every lick gives some of your health back.

quoted: Cloud N. Candy jumps during the fight, damaging the player if they touch her, and as she gets smaller, she becomes quicker and more agile. Each time she is licked, the player will recover some health.

lines.line: Summary: Skeleton dragons with several necks that stand in your way in the level Bone Dragon Pit and now and then spit a fireball.

quoted: Bone Dragons are large hydra-like dragon skeletons that Yoshis encounter in the Bone Dragon Pit in Yoshi's Story. Bone Dragons usually block a Yoshi's way
they can attack the Yoshis by occasionally spitting a fireball at them.
A three-headed skeletal dragon that shoots flames.

lines.line: Weak points: Hit a head twice with eggs, or ground-pound it twice. On the three-headed kind, every head needs its own two hits.

quoted: to get past one, the Yoshi has to either throw eggs at its head or ground-pound it, with either method taking two hits to defeat the Bone Dragon.
Each of the heads takes two hits

lines.line: Looks like: A big dragon skeleton with more than one neck, like a hydra. The three-headed kind has a body as well.

quoted: large hydra-like dragon skeletons
a Yoshi encounters a three-headed Bone Dragon, complete with a body.

lines.line: Tips: Touching the body of a three-headed one does not hurt you, and beating it earns three melons.

quoted: Touching the body does not hurt the Yoshi.
defeating the Bone Dragon earns the Yoshi three melons.

lines.line: Summary: A giant eel-like sea creature in one area of the level Lots O'Jelly Fish, which swims in circles around a Yoshi that comes near. The game treats it as a mini-boss, yet it cannot be beaten.

quoted: it is found in a single area of the level Lots O'Jelly Fish, where it waits for a Yoshi to swim nearby. When it spots them, it swims in circles around them, attempting to enclose them within its spiky body
Despite being treated as a mini-boss, it cannot be defeated

lines.line: Looks like: A large white creature with green spikes and a big fin as a tail, with a ball-shaped head that has red eyes and flippers and a long spout for a mouth.

quoted: It resembles a large white creature with green spikes and a large fin for a tail. Its head is a large ball with red eyes, flippers, and a spout for a mouth.

lines.line: Tips: You cannot throw eggs underwater, so it is practically invincible. What ends the area is defeating the Cheep Cheeps in its lair while you keep clear of it.

quoted: since Yoshis cannot throw eggs underwater, the Snorkel Snake is effectively invincible.
the Cheep Cheeps in its lair must be defeated while the Yoshi avoids it.

lines.line: Tips: Its body is too short to close a full circle, so a Yoshi it has ringed can still swim out.

quoted: its body is not long enough for it to make a complete circle, allowing the Yoshis to escape if encircled.

lines.line: Summary: A fruit that makes the Yoshi who eats it Super Happy for a short while. It turns up in bubbles, or floats down after you eat six of the same fruit in a row.

quoted: Heart Fruits can be found in bubbles; alternatively, when a Yoshi eats six of the same fruit in a row, a Heart Fruit appears from the sky and slowly floats down. When obtained, the Heart Fruit makes a Yoshi Super Happy.
Super Happy Yoshi lasts for only a limited time

lines.line: Uses: A Super Happy Yoshi is invincible and stronger, has endless eggs, a longer tongue and extra flutter-jumping, and gets the whole Smile Meter back. A ground pound pops every bubble on screen, turns Shy Guys into Lucky Fruits and peppers into coins.

quoted: In that form, he is invincible and stronger
While Super Happy, a Yoshi is given an endless supply of eggs, a longer tongue, and extra flutter-jumping
When a Yoshi transforms, his health is filled completely.
When a Yoshi ground-pounds while Super Happy, all onscreen bubbles pop, Shy Guys turn into Lucky Fruits, and peppers turn into coins.
the form's invincibility does not protect the Yoshi from fatal hazards

lines.line: Tips: The effect ends early if you eat a blue Tehee Butterfly, a Black Shy Guy or a pepper, if a Piranha Pest swallows you, or when you move on to an area that turns the page.

quoted: its effects wear off immediately if a Yoshi eats anything like a blue Tehee Butterfly, a Black Shy Guy, or a pepper or if a Yoshi is eaten by a Piranha Pest.
Moving to a new area that causes the page to turn also ends the effect early.

lines.line: Tips: Being Super Happy does not save you from the big fish called Blurps, from pits, lava or pistons.

quoted: Lastly, the form's invincibility does not protect the Yoshi from fatal hazards, such as Blurps, pits, lava, and pistons.

lines.line: Summary: Three big hearts hidden in every level. Each one you collect opens one more level on the next page.

quoted: Each stage has three Special Hearts hidden throughout the stage.
Each Special Heart opens a new level on the next page

lines.line: Uses: After the first page, only the first level of the next page is open unless you collected a Special Heart in the level you just played. You need all three to open every level on that page. Each one also heals the Yoshi fully.

quoted: only the first level of the next page can be accessed unless a Special Heart is collected in the current level; this applies to all pages past the first page.
meaning that all three Special Hearts are needed to unlock all the levels on the next page.
Unlocks a level on the next page; fully heals a Yoshi

lines.line: Tips: Chimes ring when a Baby Yoshi is close to one, and an egg can be thrown to collect one.

quoted: Ringing chimes sound when a Baby Yoshi is close to a Special Heart.
Eggs can also be thrown to collect coins and Special Hearts.

lines.line: Tips: Each Special Heart is worth 100 hearts toward Yoshi's Mood at the end of the level.

quoted: Special Hearts also boost Yoshi's Mood at the end of a stage
Special Hearts are worth 100 hearts.

lines.line: Summary: A special sunflower growing from the ground. A Baby Yoshi that eats its head is healed.

quoted: A Power Flower is a special sunflower that appears in Yoshi's Story. It grows from the ground
The head of a Power Flower can be consumed by a Baby Yoshi

lines.line: Uses: Eating the head gives back two petals of the Smile Meter. It earns no points, so it does nothing for Yoshi's Mood at the end of the level.

quoted: This allows him to recover two petals on his Smile Meter, but it does not earn him any points, unlike eating a fruit or a Shy Guy, and thus does not improve Yoshi's Mood when the stage is completed.

lines.line: Looks like: A sunflower on a green stem with green leaves. The head is yellow with red petals, black eyes and a small red mouth.

quoted: has a green stem with green leaves, as well as a yellow head with red petals, black eyes, and a small red mouth.

lines.line: Tips: The head grows back quickly after it is eaten, so you can keep eating until the Smile Meter is full.

quoted: The head of the Power Flower quickly regrows after being consumed, meaning that the Yoshi can simply keep eating flower heads until his health is fully recovered.

lines.line: Summary: A spiked fruit that grows only in the level Jungle Puddle. It tastes horrible to most Yoshis.

quoted: Bomb Berries appear only in Jungle Puddle.
An explosive spiked fruit that tastes horrible to Yoshis (except the Black and White Yoshis).

lines.line: Uses: It is a hazard, not a meal. Touching one makes the Smile Meter lose petals, and so does eating one, unless the Yoshi is the Black or the White one.

quoted: Getting in contact with a Bomb Berry causes a Yoshi to make its Smile Meter lose some petals. Eating it also causes the Yoshi to lose petals (except for the Black and White Yoshis).

lines.line: Looks like: A yellow and red aubergine-shaped fruit covered in green spikes.

quoted: Bomb Berries resemble yellow-and-red eggplants and are covered in green spikes.

lines.line: Tips: A Bomb Berry is invisible at first and swells to full size once you walk past. When it gets heavy enough it drops into the water and sinks, and after a while a new one grows in the same spot.

quoted: At first, they are invisible, but once the player walks past them, they begin to grow to full size. They continue to grow until their weight causes them to fall off into the water, where they slowly sink to the bottom. A new Bomb Berry then grows from the original spot after a while.
